adjudication.rationale: Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 7-10, the schema uses `[z.string().toString()]` as object keys. In JavaScript/TypeScript, `z.string().toString()` evaluates to a literal string (the string representation of the Zod schema), not a dynamic key pattern. This means the schema will have literal keys like '[object Object]' rather than acting as a catchall for any string key. The minimumTokenResponseSchema won't properly validate tokens with fields like 'expires_in', 'expiry_date', etc., because those computed expressions don't create dynamic property matchers in Zod - they just become literal string keys. This is a real bug that would cause token parsing to fail or strip important fields.
